if: the goods or services or both are received by a NON-RESIDENT TAXABLE PERSON
AND they are not goods imported by him
then: input tax credit is NOT AVAILABLE on them
note: The block is defined by WHO the recipient is, not by what is bought. The single carve-out is goods IMPORTED by the non-resident taxable person; domestic inward supplies to him are blocked whatever their nature, and services are not carved out at all. Section 17(5) opens 'Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) of section 16 and sub-section (1) of section 18', so this block defeats both the s.16(1) entitlement and the s.18(1) special-circumstances credit. Business use does not cure it. The source is the CGST Act as updated 31-08-2021. UNKNOWN whether a later amendment has changed this clause; later amendments are not held locally.
